_doc: Revert-verify mutants for ticket bb855bb2 / req db6b7524 (branch batch7b/create-aliases-list-guard). Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute). The production diff has TWO halves and each has its own mutant: the guard `assertAliasesAreNotAList` (wired at the top of the create action, next to the empty-label check) and the hint in CREATE_SELF_MANAGED_FLAGS, which used to print `--aliases <a,b>` — the very shape the guard now refuses, i.e. the message taught the mistake it exists to prevent. Guards are enumerated per integration-test-revert-verify §A8: the wiring (M1), the DISCRIMINATOR that keeps a human comma-space alias legal (M2), and the hint (M3). ⛤ M2 is the one that makes Y3 non-decorative: a guard reading /,/ instead of /,(?! )/ would still make Y1 pass, so without Y3 the narrow predicate would be unlocked and a later reader could 'simplify' it into rejecting `Иванов, Иван`. The predicate is not invented here — the concepts-index generator settled on the same one over the same data (build-concepts-index.py, 2026-09-14), and the req records that. Expectations were written into this file BEFORE the run (§A44).

M1_guard_not_wired._note: The pre-fix state: the helper exists but nothing calls it — the §A8 'is the new code WIRED IN' axis. Y2/Y3 stay green (they never depended on a refusal), Y4 stays green (the hint is a separate half).

M2_discriminator_widened_to_any_comma._note: Widens the guard to ANY comma, so a human alias `Иванов, Иван` is refused too. Y1 stays GREEN under it — which is the point: the narrow predicate is locked only by Y3, and without that axis this mutant would be invisible.

M3_hint_reverted_to_the_comma_form._note: Restores the hint that printed the comma-joined shape. Reddens only Y4: the guard still refuses that shape at runtime, so the other axes cannot see the message regression — which is exactly why the hint needs an axis of its own.
